'''Rebecca Caroline Thompson''' was an American physicist, popular science writer, and Chief Science and Education Officer at the [[Saint Louis Science Center]]. Her first book, ''Fire, Ice, and Physics'', explores the science of ''[[Game of Thrones]]'', and was published by [[MIT Press]] in 2019. She was elected Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]] in 2016.

== Early life and education ==
Thompson was born in [[Chicago]] and raised near [[Annapolis, Maryland]]. Her father was a physicist and her mother a high school principal.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Becky Thompson {{!}} PhysicsCentral|url=https://www.physicscentral.com/explore/people/thompson.cfm|access-date=2021-04-11|website=www.physicscentral.com | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210509024008/https://www.physicscentral.com/explore/people/thompson.cfm | archive-date=May 9, 2021 }}</ref> Thompson was encouraged by one of her friends to take a class in physics, and enjoyed it so much she decided to study it at university.<ref name=":0" /> She was the youngest person in Delaware to get her skydiving license.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|last=Biron|first=Lauren|title=Q&A: Becky Thompson|date=12 September 2019 |url=https://news.fnal.gov/2019/09/qa-becky-thompson/ | url-status=dead | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240529191131/https://news.fnal.gov/2019/09/qa-becky-thompson/ | archive-date=2024-05-29 | access-date=2021-04-11|language=en-US}}</ref>

Thompson majored in physics at [[Bryn Mawr College]]. She moved to the [[University of Texas at Austin]] for her graduate studies, where she studied pattern formation in buckled membranes using computational modeling. She worked under the supervision of [[Michael Marder]] in the Centre for Nonlinear Dynamics. Specifically, she looked at the morphology of [[Nanoflower|nano-flowers]] that form at the tip of [[silicon nanowire]]s as well as the formation of ripples in sheets of graphene.<ref>{{Cite Q|Q106466069|author=Thompson, Rebecca Caroline}}</ref> The silicon nanowire tips form nano-flowers when in the presence of different gases. In the nano-flower formation process, the nanowires extend, and intricate patterns of [[silicon oxide]] start to form.<ref name=":0" /> She has shown that the nanowires extend more in the presence of gold, and that nano-flowers only form in the presence of oxygen.<ref name=":0" /> She reported that ripples in graphene sheets can be understood by considering the adsorption of [[hydroxide]] molecules in random sites across the graphene layers.<ref name=":2">{{Cite journal|last1=Thompson-Flagg|first1=R. C.|last2=Moura|first2=M. J. B.|last3=Marder|first3=M.|date=2009|title=Rippling of graphene|journal=EPL (Europhysics Letters)|language=en|volume=85|issue=4|article-number=46002|doi=10.1209/0295-5075/85/46002|arxiv=0807.2938 |bibcode=2009EL.....8546002T |s2cid=119024976 |issn=0295-5075}}</ref> The process of adsorbing hydroxide causes the carbon – carbon bonds to extend, which can result in static buckling.<ref name=":2" /> During her graduate studies, she became more interested in teaching and doing physics outreach.<ref name=":1" />

== Career ==
In 2008, Thompson joined the [[American Physical Society]] as Head of Public Outreach. At APS, Thompson created the comic series ''Spectra: The Original Laser Superhero''.<ref name=":5">{{Cite web|date=2017-08-14|title=Thompson, Becky|url=https://apscuwip.ku.edu/thompson-rebecca|access-date=2021-04-11|website=APS CUWiP 2018 at KU|language=en}}</ref> The series, illustrated by [[Kerry G. Johnson]] and published by Physics Central,<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.physicscentral.com/experiment/physicsquest/upload/spectra-manual.pdf |title=PhysicsQuest: Spectra |last=Thompson-Flagg |first=Rebecca  |date=2010 |publisher=American Physical Society |access-date=2021-04-11 |quote=|others=Illustrated by [[Kerry G. Johnson]]}}</ref> followed a middle school student (Lucy Hene) with laser-related superpowers.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web|title=Spectra Takes on San Diego Comic-Con|url=http://www.aps.org/publications/apsnews/201808/comic-con.cfm|access-date=2021-04-11|website=www.aps.org|language=en}}</ref><ref name=":4">{{Cite web|date=2016-12-12|title=Comic Book Physics: Enlightening Science for All|url=https://www.spsnational.org/the-sps-observer/fall/2016/comic-book-physics-enlightening-science-all|access-date=2021-04-11|website=Society of Physics Students|language=en}}</ref> These included being able to pass through transparent surfaces, change colors depending on her levels of energy and play [[compact disc]]s.<ref name=":4" /> The comic book was popular amongst physicist and comic book readers, and was part of the annual [[comic book convention]] [[San Diego Comic-Con|San Diego Comi-Con]]'.<ref name=":3" /> 

Thompson contributed research and text to the American Physical Society's comic and activity book for middle school students,  ''Nikola Tesla and the Electric Fair''.<ref>{{cite web | title=Physics Quest 2008: Nikola Tesla and The Electric Fair | website=Scribd | date=March 16, 2026 | url=https://www.scribd.com/document/9632269/Physics-Quest-2008-Nikola-Tesla-and-the-Electric-Fair | access-date=March 16, 2026}}</ref>

Thompson was elected Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]] in 2016.<ref>{{Cite web|title=APS Fellow Archive|url=http://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm|access-date=2021-04-11|website=www.aps.org|language=en}}</ref> Thompson is a fan of ''[[Game of Thrones]]'', and wrote ''Fire, Ice, and Physics'', the Science of Game of Thrones for [[MIT Press]] in 2019.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Rebecca C. Thompson|url=https://mitpress.mit.edu/contributors/rebecca-c-thompson|access-date=2021-04-11|publisher=MIT Press|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|date=2019-12-08|title=Dr Rebecca Thompson and the Science of "Game of Thrones"|url=https://www.sliceofscifi.com/2019/12/07/slice-of-scifi-918/|access-date=2021-04-11|website=Slice of SciFi|language=en-US}}</ref> In 2019 Thompson joined [[Fermilab]] as Head of the Office of Education and Public Outreach.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Fermilab welcomes Rebecca Thompson as head of the Office of Education and Public Outreach|url=https://news.fnal.gov/2019/08/fermilab-welcomes-rebecca-thompson-as-head-of-the-office-of-education-and-public-outreach/|access-date=2021-04-11| url-status=dead | archive-date=2021-06-23 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210623000142/https://news.fnal.gov/2019/08/fermilab-welcomes-rebecca-thompson-as-head-of-the-office-of-education-and-public-outreach/ | language=en-US}}</ref> The [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]] selected Thompson as a fellow in 2023.<ref>{{cite news |title=2023 AAAS Fellows |url=https://www.aaas.org/fellows/2023-fellows |access-date=December 15, 2024 |publisher=American Association for the Advancement of Science}}</ref>

== Endurance sports and death ==
During her graduate studies Thompson also began doing endurance sports, completing several [[Ironman Triathlon|Ironman]] races.<ref>{{Cite web|title=2008 Ironman Arizona Results for Thompson, Becky|url=https://www.athlinks.com/event/6561/results/Event/43500/Course/64325/Bib/2102|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Physicist Takes on Superhero Role for LaserFest
|url=https://www.aps.org/archives/publications/apsnews/201001/superhero.cfm}}</ref>. In the 2020s she began to focus on open-water swimming and made concrete plans to complete the [[Triple Crown of Open Water Swimming|Triple Crown of Swimming]]: three marathon open-water swims, each more than 20 miles long with significantly challenging conditions. She completed the 20 Bridges challenge in 2025.<ref>{{Cite web|title=20 Bridges Challenge Results|url=https://www.nyopenwater.org/20-bridgesmanhattan-island-swim-solo-swim-results|language=en}}</ref>

Thompson died on July 26, 2026.<ref>{{Cite web|title=St Louis Area Masters's Post|url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/e4jPO?wr=false}}</ref>
